AllocatedUpstreamCost.description: What a product paid for one table it reads, in one unit.

low_confidence.description: The scan was so small that the proportions say little.

of_total.description: The whole cost that was split, so `amount / of_total` is the share.

provisional.description: The table has not been rebuilt since, in a month that is not over: a later reader can still change this share.

table.description: The model whose table was read.

amount.description: Whole units. Milliseconds, or byte-hours rounded down per interval.

CostSplitBasis.description: How a table version's cost was split across the models that read it.

CostUnit.description: A unit a monthly cost figure is counted in. Units are never added to each other, and the two storage bases are never added together.

DeliveryStatus.description:
Delivery state of one product deadline: was the latest delivery on time, and is the next one at risk.

Reported by `rocky product status` and, per pipeline, by the scheduler status. `on_time` and `late_by_seconds` are facts about the latest delivery. `at_risk` rests on [`DurationEstimateStatus`], and is `null` whenever the estimate is `unknown`.

at_risk.description: True when the p90 duration is longer than the time left before `next_due_at`. `null` when the estimate is `unknown`: no verdict.

last_delivered_at.description: When the latest production delivery finished.

last_due_at.description: The deadline the latest delivery served, when its run recorded one.

late_by_seconds.description: How late the latest delivery was, in seconds; `0` when on time. `null` when no delivery recorded a deadline.

next_due_at.description: The deadline the next delivery must meet. A time in the past means the next delivery is already late.

on_time.description: Whether the latest delivery met its deadline. `null` when no delivery recorded a deadline.

product.description: The product whose deadline this is.

DurationEstimateStatus.description: A p50/p90 duration estimate and the sample behind it.

basis.description: What was timed: `model_delivery` (run start to the model's finish) or `pipeline_run` (run start to run finish).

growth.description: True when the newest 5 runs were all slower than the p90 of the older ones, so `p90_ms` is the slowest of those 5.

n.description: How many production runs the estimate read.

state.description: `known` with at least 5 runs; `unknown` below that, and then no verdict rests on the estimate.

window.description: The most runs it reads (the newest 20).

oneOf.description: From run start to the product's output model finishing.
From run start to run finish, for the whole pipeline.

EstimateState.description: Whether a duration estimate has enough runs to judge from.

oneOf.description: At least 5 runs: the band is reported.
Fewer than 5 runs: no band, no verdict.

MoneyPart.description: One figure of a monthly money total.

MoneyStatus.description: Whether a money figure in the monthly report could be computed.

ProductApprovalOutput.description: The approval record, as echoed by compile/status output.

snapshot_path.description: Project-root-relative path of the immutable snapshot file.

ProductBudgetBreachAction.description: What to do when a [`ProductBudgetConfig`] limit is crossed. Only `warn` exists: the breach is reported and the `on_budget_breach` hook fires, and the run's exit code does not change.

ProductBudgetBreachEvent.description: One time a product went over its monthly budget.

at.description: When that run finished (RFC 3339). The budget was checked as of then.

breached.description: The limits that were exceeded at that run.

run_id.description: The production run after which the product was first over.

ProductBudgetCheck.description: One limit of a product budget, checked against the product's charge.

actual.description: The month-to-date figure the limit tests. Absent when it is not known.

unit.description: For `max_storage_gb_month`, the storage basis checked. Absent for the other limits.

verdict.description: `breached` when `actual` is greater than `limit`. Equal is in budget.

ProductBudgetStatus.description: A product's monthly budget, checked once.

checks.description: One check per limit set (two for `max_storage_gb_month` when both storage bases were measured).

on_breach.description: What a breach does. Only `warn`: the run's exit code does not change.

reasons.description: Why the budget as a whole is `not_evaluated`, when it is.

verdict.description: `breached` when any limit is breached. Otherwise `not_evaluated` when any limit could not be checked, or when run history does not cover the month (then always). Otherwise `in_budget`.

ProductBudgetVerdict.description: The verdict of a monthly product budget, or of one of its limits.

ProductCostMonth.description: One product's current month, on `rocky product status`.

as_of.description: The instant the month was computed (RFC 3339).

cost.description: The product's row from `rocky cost --month <month> --by product`.

history_complete.description: Whether run history reaches back far enough to cover the month.

allocated_upstream.description: What the product pays for tables it reads.

breach_events.description: Each time this month the product went over its budget, in run order. Found by checking the budget again after each production run of the month. A product that goes over, back under and over again has two events. An event is never withdrawn, even when a later run moves the product back under. Empty (and omitted) when there was none.

breach_events_skipped.description: Why `breach_events` was not computed, when it was not: the month has more production runs than the report replays (the reason gives both counts). `budget` is still checked. Absent otherwise.

budget.description: The product's `[product_budget.<name>]` checked against `charged`, as of this report. Absent when the product has no budget.

built.description: What the product's own executions cost, before any split. A memo for reading `kept` beside it: it is never summed and is not part of the invariant.

charged.description: What the product is charged: `kept` plus `allocated_upstream`.

kept.description: The part of `built` the product still pays after other products pay for what they read.

money.description: `charged` in USD, priced only from prices set in `[cost]`. Present only when `money_status` is `priced`. It covers compute and storage; egress and AI tokens are not measured and are not in it.

money_parts.description: `charged` priced one figure at a time.

money_status.description: Why `money` is or is not present.

owner_residual.description: The part of `kept` that came back from readers outside every product.

shared_not_charged.description: Shares of the product's tables that readers did not pay.

ProductSourceVolumeStatus.description: One declared source range and the latest production count of its table.

row_count.description: The table's total rows when the newest production run that counted this product's sources started. Absent when that run took no count of this table, or none has run yet.

run_id.description: The run that took the count.

table.description: The source table, as the spec lists it.

verdict.description: That count judged against the range the spec declares now: `in_range`, `below_min`, `above_max`, or `not_evaluated` when no count exists.

ProductVolumeStatus.description: The declared volume range and the latest production count.

row_count.description: The newest production build that recorded a count. Absent when no build has been counted yet.

run_id.description: The run that took the count.

verdict.description: That count judged against the range the spec declares now: `in_range`, `below_min`, `above_max`, or `not_evaluated` when no count exists.

SharedNotChargedCost.description: A share of an owned table's cost that a reader did not pay.

amount.description: The reader's share. It stays with the table's owner.

table.description: The owned model whose table was read.

VolumeSeverity.description: What an out-of-range row count does to the run.

oneOf.description: The model is marked failed after its build, and the run is partial.
The run reports a warning, and delivery is recorded as usual.

VolumeVerdict.description: The outcome of one volume check.

oneOf.description: The count is inside the range.

No count was taken, or it could not be read. Never a failure for `[product.output.volume]`. For an `error` source range, a count that could not be taken refuses the output build; a cancelled run does not.

approval.description: The approval record, when one exists.

artifact_problems.description: Byte-verification problems against the committed manifest (empty = every committed artifact matches its recorded hash).

committed_phase.description: The committed lowering phase, when a manifest exists.

committed_spec_digest.description: The committed manifest's spec digest, when one exists.

cost_month.description: The product's cost for the current month (in the project's `[schedule].timezone`), with its `[product_budget.<name>]` verdict and breach events when it has a budget: its row from `rocky cost --month <month> --by product`. Present only from `rocky product status` (and the same route of `rocky serve`), only for a product that has a `[product_budget.<name>]`, whose spec parses and that owns a model.

cost_month_error.description: Why `cost_month` could not be computed, when it could not.

delivery.description: Delivery state, when the spec declares `deliver_by`: whether the latest production delivery was on time, how late, and whether the next delivery is at risk. The estimate times run start to the output model's finish.

fulfill_state.description: The persisted fulfillment state tag, when one exists.

journal_rows.description: Number of fulfillment journal rows recorded for this product.

output_model.description: The resolved output model, when the spec parses.

product.description: The product name the status was asked for.

snapshot_intact.description: Whether the approval snapshot's bytes still digest to the recorded value. `null` without an approval; `false` is tamper.

source_volumes.description: Source range state, one row per `[[product.source.volume]]` the spec declares: the range and the count the newest production run that counted this product's sources took at its start. Empty (and omitted) when the spec declares no source range.

spec_digest.description: The working spec's digest, when it parses.

spec_error.description: Why the spec failed to parse, when it did not.

spec_matches_approval.description: Whether the working spec equals the approved revision. `null` when either side is missing.

staging_journal_present.description: Whether an uncommitted staging journal is pending. Status never mutates; the next compile resolves it.

volume.description: Volume state, when the spec declares `[product.output.volume]`: the declared range and the latest production count judged against it.
